- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot recent high prices, then sharply drop below true values.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: after a spike, it underpredicts the subsequent decline, then overcorrects.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the 30d window.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Overestimation is more pronounced when true values are trending downward; model underestimates the depth of the drop.
- Model tends to ignore recent low prices in the history window, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then become overly pessimistic in the last 10 days.
- Model does not adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns in the 30d history, leading to persistent bias.
- When true values are near or below 65, model forecasts remain above 70, indicating a hard floor bias.
